misconceptions.description: Assembling an evaluation brief as disconnected sections that never link back to one decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner stacks sections without showing how they support the recommendation
misconceptions.feedback: Link the parts: the recommendation should answer the original question, and the evidence, equity, cost, and fit sections should each justify it.

misconceptions.description: Treating synthesis as hiding the conflict between sections rather than naming and resolving it
misconceptions.trigger: learner drops or buries a section that conflicts with the preferred conclusion
misconceptions.feedback: Surface the tension between sections and explain which consideration was prioritized and why. A visible trade-off is stronger than a clean-looking brief.

misconceptions.description: Submitting an AI-assembled capstone brief without verifying each claim against the learner's own evidence
misconceptions.trigger: learner forwards a fluent AI assembly as their brief
misconceptions.feedback: Use the AI assembly as a draft. Verify that every claim traces to your own evidence and that the recommendation is one you can defend.

misconceptions.description: Treating a polished, complete brief as a closed decision with no stated condition that would change the recommendation
misconceptions.trigger: learner omits what evidence would overturn the conclusion
misconceptions.feedback: Name what could change the recommendation. A decision that cannot say what would change its mind is an assertion, not an inspectable judgment.
